subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu text commands (/stop, /new, /status) no longer bypass queue during active agent run (3.8 regression)

question: Should Feishu whole-message text commands during active runs be limited to the safe local fast-path subset, or should stateful commands such as `/stop` and `/new` also become authorized text-slash turns that bypass active-run queueing?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses command authorization, session mutation, and per-chat ordering semantics; automation can implement the chosen boundary but should not pick it implicitly.

options.title: Choose Broad Feishu Text-Command Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the stateful-command boundary and then sponsor a focused Feishu/core fix with live DM proof.

options.title: Limit To Safe Local Commands
options.body: Keep only low-risk operational commands such as `/status` on the fast path and track `/stop` and `/new` as a separate explicit design decision.

options.title: Restore Every Reported Command
options.body: Treat `/status`, `/stop`, and `/new` as authorized text-slash command turns with queue bypass, backed by Feishu active-run tests and live evidence.

recommendation.title: Choose Broad Feishu Text-Command Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the stateful-command boundary and then sponsor a focused Feishu/core fix with live DM proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for command authorization and command-turn policy is on steipete-authored commits, and the choice spans security-sensitive command behavior.
